title: Actuator
description: What drives a joint. The one field that matters most is the one datasheets rarely publish: continuous_torque_nm. A hobby servo's headline number is stall torque - what it produces at the instant it stops moving, drawing a current it cannot sustain - and a model that reads it as capacity will confidently specify a mechanism that overheats. Only the continuous figure feeds a capacity derivation (ADR-0004).

part_id.description: The OpenPartsCore entry for this actuator, if it has one. Stored, not resolved (ADR-0006).

type.description: hobby-servo takes a PWM pulse and reports nothing. smart-servo has a bus and position feedback. The distinction matters for what a controller can know, not only for what the motor can do.

stall_torque_nm.description: The datasheet headline, as a CURVE SAMPLED AT VOLTAGES rather than one figure (ADR-0014). Recorded because datasheets publish it and omitting the field invites someone to write it into continuous_torque_nm, NOT because it is usable. A validator must refuse to let these values reach a capacity derivation (ADR-0004).

continuous_torque_nm.description: The only torque that may feed a capacity derivation, and an array for the reason ADR-0014 gives: torque against voltage is a curve, and this actuator's own rated range can span 26%. Null means capacity cannot be derived and the answer is 'incomplete', naming this actuator - the same shape as OpenBuildCore answering 'requires slicing' for a machine with no measured throughput (its ADR-0005). Most hobby datasheets do not publish this, so null will be the common case; that is a true statement about the available evidence, not a gap to be filled with a fraction of stall torque.

how_determined.description: Datasheet continuous rating, or a measurement and its method. A rule of thumb applied to stall torque is not a determination and must be rejected here - it is a guess wearing a citation.

thermal_basis.description: Duty cycle, ambient, and whether steady state was reached. A torque held for ten seconds is not a continuous torque.

no_load_speed_rad_s.description: Also voltage-indexed (ADR-0014): the same datasheet that publishes three torque rows publishes three speed rows, from the same table.

travel.description: The actuator's own travel, before any gearing. Distinct from the joint limits in the robot record: those are what the mechanism permits, this is what the motor can do. A capacity or reachability derivation takes the tighter of the two.

backlash_rad.description: Absent means UNKNOWN, never zero. Backlash is why a commanded pose and an achieved pose differ, and recording it as zero because nobody measured it is the invented-data failure in miniature. NOTE: trade sources report there is no standard governing how backlash is measured - averaging methods and applied torques differ between vendors - which would make two vendors' figures incomparable without their methods. That claim is SECONDARY-SOURCED and no rule is built on it yet (ADR-0018).

measured_efficiency.description: Replaces a scalar efficiency field, which was the third instance of this repo's recurring defect: a quantity varying over an operating envelope, stored as one number (ADR-0018). Harmonic Drive's own engineering data states efficiency 'varies depending on input speed, ratio, load level, temperature, and type of lubrication' and publishes eight curves and no scalar - and its worked example lands at 58% at rated load and 50% at 60% of rated, against the 80-90% the trade literature quotes. STILL FEEDS NO DERIVATION, and now for a sourced reason rather than an unmodelled one: efficiency curves describe a gearbox that is TURNING, indexed by input speed, while a static hold has an input speed of zero. Applying a running efficiency to a held pose is wrong in kind, not in value. A vendor curve may be sampled into this array; a single catalogue number may not, because there is no such thing.

input_speed_rad_s.description: The operating point this figure was read at. Required, because it is the primary index of every published efficiency curve.

output_torque_nm.description: Efficiency falls with load below rated; a figure without its load is not a figure.

lubricant.description: Named grease or oil, and quantity where the vendor conditions the curve on it. Harmonic Drive's curves are valid only for their own grease at standard quantity.

how_determined.description: Read from which chart of which document, or measured how. Reading a value off a chart image is not a citation and should say so.

feedback.description: 'none' is a real answer and a consequential one: an open-loop actuator cannot confirm it reached a commanded pose, so anything derived about where the mechanism actually is becomes an assumption.

stall_current_a.description: Sizing a supply from no-load current is how a mechanism browns out the moment it takes a load.

mass_g.description: An actuator mounted partway along a chain is itself a load on every joint below it.

basis.description: Whether this value describes the PRODUCT LINE or the object on your bench (ADR-0018). The distinction is not pedantry: Harmonic Drive states in a datasheet that its published torsional stiffness is 'the average of many tests of actual units' and that 'the spring rate of an individual unit may vary within approximately +/-30% of the average'. A cited value has meant 'somebody published it' everywhere in this platform so far; this is a vendor saying their number describes a population. ABSENT MEANS UNKNOWN, never 'assumed exact' - and a derivation must report the weakest basis it consumed, because a verdict built from population averages is a different claim from one built from measurements of the specific hardware.

spreadPct.description: Unit-to-unit variation the vendor states for a model-typical figure, as a percentage of the value. Only ever a figure somebody published; absent means the spread is UNKNOWN, not zero.

torqueAtVolts.description: One row of a published table. Voltage is not an annotation on the value - it is the index the value is looked up by, and a derivation that picks the wrong row is wrong by the width of the curve (ADR-0014).

at_volts.description: Required. A torque or speed figure without its supply voltage is not a figure - the same servo quoted at 6.0 V and 7.4 V differs substantially, and the XM430 spans 26% across its own rated range.

at_amps.description: Current drawn at this row, where the datasheet states it. Sizing a supply from no-load current is how a mechanism browns out the moment it takes a load.
